references.title: A. Blokhuis, A. E. Brouwer, B. M. M. de Weger, Binomial collisions and near collisions, Integers 17 (2017) #A64

literature_proposed.summary: Known by computation: Blokhuis, Brouwer and de Weger searched every row n ≤ 10^6 of the half triangle and found no collision beyond the eight sporadic quadruples and Lind's family (Theorem 2.2). A finite but large verification; a formalisation would be a certified computation, not a proof from the literature's argument.

review.words: Is it true that, for every integer $t\geq1$, there is some integer $a$ such that ${n \choose k} = a$ with $1\leq k \le \frac{n}{2}$ has exactly $t$ solutions?
